identity.name: Republika Srpska
alt_names: Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Republic of the Serb People of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina

land.text: the Serb-held regions of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which the Assembly of the Serb People proclaimed on 9 January 1992 as part of 'Yugoslavia'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Yugoslavia row ends 1991; the Bosnian dossier opens in March 1992.

land.text: Republika Srpska as drawn at Dayton, 'one of its two main' divisions of the state under Annex 4

successors.note: From 14 December 1995 the land is an entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina (Dayton Annex 2 sets the inter-entity boundary). The entity's later life (to 2026) is not a separate dossier: see notes.

capitals.name: Banja Luka
capitals.note: The page has the Serb deputies' assembly declaring the severance of ties 'in Banja Luka' on 6-7 April 1992 and Serbs meeting there on 13 October 1990; it names no capital for the war years. The wartime seat at Pale is not on the pages read. Coordinates are the city's.

correction.text: the land the Bosnian Serbs held, drawn as Republika Srpska at Dayton (infobox 24,641 km2, 48% of the country excluding Brčko)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Bosnian War page says the Serbs 'seized control of approximately 70% of the country's territory' in 1992 and gives no map of the fronts by year; the Dayton shape (infobox 24,641 km2; 24,816.2 km2 without Brčko; 48% of Bosnia) is used for all four years, as the Bosnian dossier's contest zone does. Natural Earth spells the entity 'Repuplika Srpska'.

region.text: the Serb-held regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina

ledger.note: 9 January 1992: the Bosnian Serbs proclaim their republic. 'The assembly proclaimed the Republic of the Serb People of Bosnia and Herzegovina, declaring it part of Yugoslavia' on 9 January 1992, after the Assembly of the Serb People was formed on 24 October 1991 and a plebiscite on 9-10 November 1991 (96% for a Yugoslav federation with Serbia and Montenegro). The constitution followed on 28 February 1992.

region.text: the land the Bosnian Serbs seized, Republika Srpska as drawn at Dayton

ledger.note: 6 April 1992: the Bosnian War begins and the Serbs take much of the country. 'Serb forces began shelling Sarajevo' on 6 April 1992 and the Bosnian Serb forces, supported by the JNA, 'seized control of approximately 70% of the country's territory' over the following months. The Republika Srpska page adds that the European Community recognised Bosnia and Herzegovina on 6 April and that the Banja Luka assembly declared a severance of governmental ties the same day.
12 August 1992: the Serb republic takes the name Republika Srpska. 'The name Republika Srpska was adopted on 12 August 1992.'

region.text: Republika Srpska as drawn at Dayton

ledger.note: 21 November 1995: the Dayton talks end the war. Ceasefires were agreed on 14 September and 5 October 1995; the talks ran at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base from 1 to 21 November and the agreement 'was initialled on 21 November'.

region.text: Republika Srpska as an entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina

ledger.note: 14 December 1995: the Dayton Agreement is signed in Paris and Republika Srpska becomes an entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 'Annex 4 became the constitution, recognising Republika Srpska as one of its two main' political-territorial divisions; Annex 2 set the inter-entity boundary lines.

wars.name: Bosnian War

zones.text: the Serb-held land, Republika Srpska as drawn at Dayton

wars.outcome: Ended by the Dayton Agreement (initialled 21 November, signed 14 December 1995), which made Republika Srpska one of two entities of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Srebrenica fell in July 1995 and more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys were killed there.
wars.note: The page gives the Serb share only for 1992 (about 70%); the 1993-95 front lines, Operation Deliberate Force and the Vance-Owen plan (rejected by a Republika Srpska referendum on 15-16 May 1993) are not territorial events on the pages read.

certainty.note: Front lines, not borders, until the Dayton inter-entity boundary (Annex 2); the pages give no yearly maps.

sources.title: Republika Srpska
sources.note: Proclamation 9 January 1992, name 12 August 1992, Dayton 14 December 1995, area figures; no capital, leaders or Pale on the page.

sources.title: Bosnian War
sources.note: 6 April 1992, 70% share, ceasefires, Dayton 21 November, Herzeg-Bosnia 18 November 1991, Western Bosnia as belligerent.

notes: Requested as a counterpart by eu-22-e (bosnia-and-herzegovina). Modelled as a rebel state for 1992-1995 so that the mirror events match the Bosnian dossier's contest_start (April 1992), contest_end (November 1995) and gain (14 December 1995). The entity after Dayton (24,641 km2, to 2026; Brčko District made in 2000, the page is silent on that; the army abolished 1 January 2006; Dodik's 2025 conviction) is an internal division of Bosnia and Herzegovina and has no dossier type of its own; if the site wants the two entities drawn, the orchestrator needs an 'entity' type or the Federation and the Republic as two sub-states of the Bosnian dossier. Not settled: the by-year front lines (about 70% in 1992, 49% at Dayton), the Serb Autonomous Oblasts of 1991 (not on the pages), the seat at Pale, the leaders (Karadžić, Plavšić, Krajišnik are not on the pages read), the Union with the Republic of Serbian Krajina (not on the page), the Brčko arbitration. Gazetteer: the Natural Earth entity name is 'Repuplika Srpska'.
